chapters.summary: Council staff calls the room to order, reminds attendees to silence electronic devices, and instructs that no one may approach the dais. Chair Schulman is confirmed as ready to begin the vote meeting of the Committee on Health. [0:00:00-0:01:51
chapters.title: Staff housekeeping announcements before Health Committee vote

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We are getting ready to start.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And welcome to today's New York City Council vote from the Committee on Health.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, I'd like to remind everyone to please silence their electronic devices, and at no point is anyone to approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: My name is Lynn Schulman, chair of the New York City Council's Committee on Health.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I want to welcome all of you to today's vote.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: We've been joined by the following council members.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Felder, Wilson, Narcisse, De La Rosa, anybody else?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Today we'll be voting on two pieces of legislation, both sponsored by Councilmember Oswald Feliz.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The first is proposed introduction 196C, which would modify the sodium warning used by chain restaurants of 15 or more locations.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The second is proposed introduction 547B, which would modify the required icon for added sugar warnings.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: As we all know, consuming too much sodium or sugar can have serious consequences for our health.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Health experts tell us that the average person only needs to consume about 1,500 milligrams of sodium every day.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Over time, too much sodium can contribute to high blood pressure and increase the risk of heart disease and stroke.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The same is true when it comes to added sugar.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Experts recommend not consuming more than 200 calories or about 12 teaspoons of sugar in a day.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The average American is consuming about 17 teaspoons a day or 270 calories.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Over time, too much sugar can increase bad cholesterol, which can increase the risk of serious health conditions such as type 2 diabetes and heart disease.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: New Yorkers deserve clear and easily understandable information about what is in the food they eat.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: These warnings are a simple but important tool that can help people make informed decisions about their health.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: As our city continues to reduce the rate of deaths from heart and diabetes-related diseases as part of its healthy NYC goals, the council must ensure that New Yorkers have the information they need to make educated, health-conscious choices about their diets.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I want to thank the speaker, committee staff, my staff, and my colleagues for all their hard work and support.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And finally, I want to thank Councilmember Feliz for his leadership and dedication to this issue.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: With that, I pass it to the clerk to call the roll.

utterances.speaker: Ben Jacobs
utterances.text: Roll call vote for intro 196C and intro 547B.

utterances.speaker: Ben Jacobs
utterances.text: That's a vote of seven in the affirmative with none in the negative and no abstentions.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I also want to recognize Councilmember Areola on Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Ben Jacobs
utterances.text: The vote will be held open.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: The health committee hearing is now closed out.

title: Committee on Health
topic: Modifying the sodium warning at designated food service establishments
